WorldFloraFast

Website: https://jeromechave.github.io/WorldFloraFast/

Fast matching of plant names against the World Flora Online (WFO) taxonomic backbone. A refactored derivative of WorldFlora (Kindt 2020, Applications in Plant Sciences 8: e11388) with the same functions and arguments, 10-15x faster fuzzy matching, and much faster exact matching on large inputs (see below), plus the corrections listed in NEWS.md.

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jeromechave/WorldFloraFast",
                        dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)
library(WorldFloraFast)

WFO.download()        # latest WFO Plant List (2026-06) from Zenodo, to a per-user data folder; loads WFO.data
res <- WFO.match(c("Faidherbia albida", "Acacia nilotca", "Compositae"), WFO.data = WFO.data)
# optional matching steps for difficult names
res2 <- WFO.match(c("Reinwardtiod cinerum", "Palma colorada"), WFO.data = WFO.data,
                  Fuzzy.genus = TRUE, Fuzzy.transfer = TRUE, Fuzzy.one.strict = TRUE)
one <- WFO.one(res)                         # one row per submitted name

# later sessions
WFO.remember()                              # reload the remembered backbone as WFO.data
WFO.download(update = TRUE)   # check for a newer release
WFO.releases()                # releases downloaded, and where

Works with the WFO Plant List 2026-06 and earlier releases. By default it behaves as WorldFlora (same arguments and result columns), with errors corrected: a correctly spelled genus is kept, short epithets are not replaced, and placeholders such as “indet.” are not matched. Optional matching steps (Fuzzy.genus, Fuzzy.transfer, Fuzzy.one.strict) handle truncated genera (“Reinwardtiod cinerum”), species moved to another genus (“Chrysophyllum madagascariensis” -> Gambeya boiviniana), short epithets, and local names such as “Palma colorada”, which are then not given a scientific genus.

Functions

Task Functions
Get the backbone WFO.download(), WFO.read(), WFO.remember()
Separate names and authors WFO.prepare(), WFO.preprepare()
Match names WFO.match()
One match per name WFO.one()
Explore WFO.browse(), WFO.synonyms(), WFO.family(), WFO.url()
Check fuzzy matches WFO.spelling.check()
Other backbones WFO.backbone() (WorldFlora name: new.backbone())

Start with vignette("WorldFloraFast"); news(package = "WorldFloraFast") lists the differences with WorldFlora.

Speed

On the WFO Plant List 2026-06 (1.66 million names), one core:

Task Time
50,000 records of correctly spelled names (5,000 distinct) 5 s
200 misspelled names 59 s (0.3 s per name)
a further call on the same backbone, one name under 0.5 s

The first call of a session also builds the index of the backbone (about 5 s). Compared with WorldFlora 1.14-5 on a backbone of 1.37 million names: 600 correctly spelled names 51 s -> under 3 s; misspelled names about 4 s -> 0.3 s each. Use cores = n in WFO.match() for large sets of misspelled names (Linux, macOS).

How it is faster without changing results

  • The backbone is indexed once; all lookups are hash lookups instead of full-table scans.
  • Each distinct name is fuzzy-matched once, however often it occurs.
  • Before each agrep() search, an exact pigeonhole prefilter discards names that cannot match: with at most k edits, one of k + 1 pieces of the name must occur unchanged.
  • All post-processing is vectorised.

Validation

Outputs were compared record by record with WorldFlora 1.14-5 on the same data under 8 option settings of WFO.match() (with the new matching steps switched off), 5 of WFO.one(), and for WFO.prepare(), WFO.browse() and the other functions. With the optional steps, a sample of 1,137 names of the WFO Plant List 2026-06 with known answers is matched correctly for all 1,000 exact names, all 60 names with a typo and 38 of 40 names with a truncated genus. Every difference is one of the documented corrections in NEWS.md. Unit tests in tests/ cover each correction.
